BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.

content.text:
Rule 1 satisfied: 9 passing, 0 failing.

**Naming Evaluation (first priority)**

- `policyBasePremium` — computes the policy's base premium from items. Name still fits.
- `BLOCK_SIZE` / `BLOCK_BASE_PREMIUM` — the spec calls this a "building block of 3 alike components". `BLOCK_SIZE` is fine; `BLOCK_BASE_PREMIUM` is accurate.
- `itemBasePremium`, `withFirstInsuranceSurcharge`, `roundInMHPCOsFavor`, `quotePremium` — all reveal intent well.
- The one weak spot: `policyBasePremium` currently has a **hidden precondition** in its name. It says "block applies when `items.length === BLOCK_SIZE`", but the spec's rule is "3 **alike** components". The current code passes tests only because both block tests use 3 identical runes. That's honest minimal implementation (the "different types" case is still `it.todo`), so I won't implement ahead — but the shape can be made to reveal intent better.

**APP Mass — before**

```
const policyBasePremium = (items: Item[]): number => {
  if (items.length === BLOCK_SIZE) {
    return BLOCK_BASE_PREMIUM;
  }
  return items.reduce((sum, item) => sum + itemBasePremium(item), 0);
};
```

| Component | Count | Mass |
|---|---|---|
| Bindings (`items`, `sum`, `item`) | 3 | 3 |
| Invocations (`.length`, `===`, `reduce`, `itemBasePremium`, `+`) | 5 | 10 |
| Conditionals (`if`) | 1 | 4 |
| Loops (`reduce`) | 1 | 5 |
| Constants (`BLOCK_SIZE`, `BLOCK_BASE_PREMIUM` refs) | 2 | 2 |

**Total: 24**

**Refactoring applied (Rule 2 — reveals intent)**

Extracted the two branches into named concepts so the conditional reads as a rule rather than a length check, and the summation gets its own name.

content.text:
Still green — 9 passing.

**APP Mass — after**

`formsBuildingBlock`: bindings 1 + invocations 2 (`.length`, `===`) = 4 + constant 1 → **6**
`sumOfItemBasePremiums`: bindings 3 + invocations 3 (`reduce`, `itemBasePremium`, `+`) = 6 + loop 5 + constant 1 (`0`) → **15**
`policyBasePremium`: binding 1 + invocations 3 (`formsBuildingBlock`, `sumOfItemBasePremiums`) = 4 + conditional (ternary) 4 + constant 1 → **10**

**Total: 31** (was 24, Δ +7)

Mass went **up**, and I kept the change anyway. Per the priority ordering, Rule 2 (reveals intent) outranks APP, and the win here is that `policyBasePremium` now reads as the business rule itself — *a building block prices as a block, otherwise sum the parts* — in a single expression, instead of an anonymous length comparison mixed with an inline fold. The extra mass is entirely the two invocation hops introduced by naming the concepts. I want to flag that as a judgement call rather than a measured improvement, since the metric argues against it: if you'd rather keep mass down at nine tests in, reverting to the single-function form is defensible and I'd not object.

The naming extraction also puts the predicate where the real rule will land. Right now `formsBuildingBlock` only checks `items.length === BLOCK_SIZE`, which is **not** the spec's rule — the spec says three *alike* components. The current code passes only because both block tests use three identical runes; `2 runes + 1 moonstone` (still `it.todo`) will fail against it, as will `3 runes + 3 moonstones`. I deliberately did not fix that, since implementing ahead of the tests is out of scope for refactor, but the false-green is worth naming explicitly: `formsBuildingBlock` currently over-claims relative to what it verifies.

Rules 3 and 4 found nothing actionable. No duplication exists across the pricing helpers, and every element is reachable from `quotePremium`; the `Damage`/`Incident`/`ClaimStep` types are unused so far but are spec-driven scaffolding for the claim tests, not dead code to strip.
